subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw restore cross-machine Chrome extension relay support as a maintained profile driver/plugin path, or keep it retired until a browser-backend Plugin SDK seam and security model are designed?
rationale: This choice controls remote browser-control authority over signed-in sessions and a public config/API surface, so automation cannot safely decide it by restoring the old driver string.

options.title: Design secure plugin/API seam
options.body: Define the browser backend contract, relay permissions, auth, tab ownership, audit logging, migration, and tests before accepting an optional relay implementation.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Treat existing-session, browser node, and remote CDP as the supported paths and document why the extension relay is no longer a supported OpenClaw runtime path.

options.title: Restore a first-party relay driver
options.body: Bring back a maintained `extension` driver directly in the browser plugin, accepting core ownership of the relay lifecycle and security boundary.

recommendation.title: Design secure plugin/API seam
recommendation.body: Define the browser backend contract, relay permissions, auth, tab ownership, audit logging, migration, and tests before accepting an optional relay implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the strongest recent history for the removal and migration that created this compatibility and security decision.
